mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 20-day returns in more than 60% of instances where this trigger is met, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate revenue expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND HOUST monthly change < -5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 achieves positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the average return is not significantly negative at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for three consecutive months is associated with reduced consumer spending power, leading to lower earnings for cyclically sensitive sectors and negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly negative during such episodes, or the trigger fires but more than 50% of returns are positive.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% while the unemployment rate is below 6% signals supply-side disruptions in a tight labor market, which raises input costs and reduces margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with supply shock
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered months, or the average return is not significantly below zero at 90% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A rapid deceleration in core CPI (CPIAUCSL) below 1.5% while the federal funds rate remains above 3.5% for three months signals a disinflationary environment with restrictive policy, which increases risk aversion and yields negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL < 1.5% for three consecutive months AND FEDFUNDS > 3.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 95% confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (proxied by RSAFS growth > 5% YoY) alongside a decline in personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces demand and is associated with negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS YoY growth > 5% AND GDPC1 YoY growth < 0%
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are not significantly negative in these episodes, or positive returns occur more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% while the unemployment rate is below 5% signals a tight labor market, which boosts wage pressures and input costs, ultimately leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher earnings expectations.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive in triggered months, or more than 50% of episodes result in negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) of more than 5% for four consecutive months signals a recovery in residential investment, which boosts construction-related earnings and supports positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are not significantly positive during periods of sustained HOUST increases, or the median return is not above the baseline at 90% confidence.
